title: The section component locus admits local smooth noetherian models
statement: Let g:P→T be smooth, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with a section σ satisfying σ≫g=id. For every x∈P there is an open W containing x, schemes P₀,T₀ with T₀ noetherian, a smooth quasi-compact quasi-separated g₀:P₀→T₀ with a section σ₀, and a scheme morphism a:W→P₀ such that, for every w∈W, w belongs to the component of σ(g(w)) in its g-fibre if and only if a(w) belongs to the component of σ₀(g₀(a(w))) in its g₀-fibre.

source.place: Tag 055Q, first two paragraphs (noetherian approximation), and Tag 055M (base change)

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood V of g(x) and W=g⁻¹(V). Restrict the section and finitely presented smooth morphism to V; this leaves each fibre and its section point unchanged.

Descend the restricted morphism and section to a finitely generated Z-algebra. Increase the stage to descend the section identity and smoothness. The resulting base T₀ is noetherian and the morphism g₀ is finitely presented, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The base-change projection gives a:W→P₀.

The connected component of the section point in each fibre is geometrically connected. Base change therefore preserves precisely that component (Tag 055M). This gives the membership equivalence for every w.
